deltas.question: What is a morphism in category theory?
What is the difference between a monomorphism and an epimorphism?
What is an isomorphism in category theory?
What is an endomorphism and how does it differ from an automorphism?
deltas.gemma_answer: function mapping a path to a vector
deltas.canonical_answer: endomorphism = morphism f:A→A; automorphism = invertible endomorphism; automorphisms form a group

deltas.question: What is a functor and how does it map morphisms?
What is a natural transformation between two functors?
deltas.gemma_answer: confused functor and natural transformation — said nat trans is just a higher-level functor
deltas.canonical_answer: η:F⇒G assigns η_A:FA→GA to each object A; naturality square η_B∘F(f)=G(f)∘η_A

deltas.question: Is every isomorphism both a monomorphism and an epimorphism?
deltas.gemma_answer: not necessarily — isomorphism is invertible but mono/epi are separate properties
deltas.canonical_answer: YES — every isomorphism is both monic and epic; converse fails (ℤ→ℚ in rings)

deltas.question: What is a fixed point of a function?
What is the Y combinator and what does it compute?
What is Banach's fixed point theorem?
deltas.gemma_answer: sequences on compact metric space converge to limits that are fixed points
deltas.canonical_answer: contraction mapping on complete metric space: unique fixed point, converge from any start

deltas.question: What is the difference between the least and greatest fixed points?
deltas.gemma_answer: least is closest to zero, greatest is furthest from zero
deltas.canonical_answer: µF=lfp iterate F from ⊥ inductive finite; νF=gfp coinductive infinite streams anamorphism

deltas.question: How does Kleene's fixed point theorem build the least fixed point?
deltas.gemma_answer: iterates from bottom element, builds up through chain
deltas.canonical_answer: µf=⊔{f^n(⊥)|n≥0} — sup of chain on CPO; base of denotational semantics for recursion

deltas.question: What is Lawvere's fixed point theorem?
deltas.gemma_answer: surjective map from set to function space implies every self-map has fixed point
deltas.canonical_answer: in CCC: point-surjective transpose ε:A×A→Y implies every f:Y→Y has fixed point; unifies Cantor/Gödel/halting

deltas.question: Is the Y combinator typeable in the simply typed lambda calculus?
deltas.gemma_answer: partial — acknowledged not typeable but missed why STLC is strongly normalising
deltas.canonical_answer: NO — λx.f(xx) needs x:τ and x:τ→σ; impossible in STLC; STLC strongly normalising = no general recursion
